spec.description: CMU's package-delivery quadcopter, 209 flights: replay one on the fleet layer with its height, speed, power and voltage, and compare the energy per kilometre of all of them against speed, payload and wind.

options.content:
### One delivery drone, 209 flights

Carnegie Mellon flew a **DJI Matrice 100** quadcopter autonomously around Pittsburgh between April and October 2019 to measure what a small-package delivery costs in energy. Each flight was set up with a **route**, a **commanded speed**, a **payload** and a **cruise altitude**; the drone logged its GPS position, orientation, battery voltage and current and the wind (from an anemometer on board) about five times a second.

Pick a flight above, or click one in the table at the bottom. The **map** replays it on the fleet layer: the drone flies at its real height, turned to its heading, with its trail coloured by battery power. The curves on the left follow the map's time bar. **Comparing the flights** puts the picked one among all the others: how much energy a kilometre takes against speed, payload and wind.

It is one drone, not a fleet: every flight here is the same aircraft. Data: Rodrigues, Patrikar, Choudhry, Feldgoise, Arcot, Gahlaut, Lau, Moon, Wagner, Matthews, Scherer and Samaras, *In-flight positional and energy use data set of a DJI Matrice 100 quadcopter for small package delivery*, Scientific Data 8, 155 (2021) — [KiltHub](https://kilthub.cmu.edu/articles/dataset/Data_Collected_with_Package_Delivery_Quadcopter_Drone/12683453), CC BY 4.0. The server reads the 107 MB file once a month through its cache and DuckDB sends the browser only the flight on screen and one row per flight; Chaski answers every panel from there.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT flight::INTEGER AS "Flight", takeoff AS "Take-off", route AS "Route", speed_ms AS "Speed",
       payload_g::INTEGER AS "Payload", altitude_m AS "Altitude", duration_s AS "Duration",
       distance_m AS "Distance", energy_wh AS "Energy", wh_per_km AS "Energy per km",
       wind_ms AS "Mean wind", max_height_m AS "Highest"
FROM $flights ORDER BY flight

spec.description: Click a row to show that flight above. Routes: R1 is the main delivery loop (most flights); R2 to R7 other loops; A1 to A3 altitude tests and H hovering, which barely move. Altitude: the commanded cruise altitude.
spec.title: All flights

spec.description: Energy is battery voltage × current over the flight, take-off and landing included. Highest: metres above the take-off point. Mean wind: from the anemometer on board, so it includes the airflow of the drone's own motion.
spec.title: The picked flight

spec.description: The picked flight on the fleet layer, at its real height above the take-off point and turned to its heading. The trail is coloured by battery power. Play or drag the time bar: the curves on the left mark the same moment.
spec.title: Flight replay

spec.rawSql:
WITH pos AS (
  SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $track WHERE time <= try_cast(rtrim($brush_to, 'Z') AS TIMESTAMP)
)
SELECT elapsed_s AS "Seconds since take-off", height_m AS "Height (m)",
       CASE WHEN time = pos.t THEN height_m END AS "Map position"
FROM $track, pos
ORDER BY elapsed_s

spec.description: Metres above the take-off point, from GPS altitude: a few metres of noise near the ground.
spec.title: Height (m)

spec.rawSql:
WITH pos AS (
  SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $track WHERE time <= try_cast(rtrim($brush_to, 'Z') AS TIMESTAMP)
)
SELECT elapsed_s AS "Seconds since take-off", speed_kmh AS "Ground speed (km/h)",
       CASE WHEN time = pos.t THEN speed_kmh END AS "Map position"
FROM $track, pos
ORDER BY elapsed_s

spec.description: Horizontal speed from the velocity the drone reports.
spec.title: Ground speed (km/h)

spec.rawSql:
WITH pos AS (
  SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $track WHERE time <= try_cast(rtrim($brush_to, 'Z') AS TIMESTAMP)
)
SELECT elapsed_s AS "Seconds since take-off", power_w AS "Battery power (W)",
       CASE WHEN time = pos.t THEN power_w END AS "Map position"
FROM $track, pos
ORDER BY elapsed_s

spec.description: Voltage × current. Climbing and hovering cost the most; cruise is cheaper per second, and faster cruise cheaper per kilometre.
spec.title: Battery power (W)

spec.rawSql:
WITH pos AS (
  SELECT max(time) AS t FROM $track WHERE time <= try_cast(rtrim($brush_to, 'Z') AS TIMESTAMP)
)
SELECT elapsed_s AS "Seconds since take-off", voltage_v AS "Battery voltage (V)",
       CASE WHEN time = pos.t THEN voltage_v END AS "Map position"
FROM $track, pos
ORDER BY elapsed_s

spec.description: The 6-cell pack under load: it sags when the motors draw hard and recovers on landing.
spec.title: Battery voltage (V)

spec.rawSql:
-- Flights that cruised (speed above 0), one point each, coloured by payload.
-- The picked flight is drawn again on top.
SELECT speed_ms AS "Commanded speed",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 0 THEN wh_per_km END AS "No payload",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 250 THEN wh_per_km END AS "250 g",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 500 THEN wh_per_km END AS "500 g",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 750 THEN wh_per_km END AS "750 g",
  CASE WHEN flight = ${flight:raw} THEN wh_per_km END AS "Picked flight"
FROM $flights WHERE wh_per_km IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 1

spec.description: Each point a flight that cruised (the hover and altitude tests, at speed 0, are left out). A quadcopter spends most of its energy staying up, so the faster it covers the route the less each kilometre costs; payload lifts the whole curve.
spec.title: Energy per km against commanded speed

spec.rawSql:
SELECT wind_ms AS "Mean wind",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 0 THEN wh_per_km END AS "No payload",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 250 THEN wh_per_km END AS "250 g",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 500 THEN wh_per_km END AS "500 g",
  CASE WHEN payload_g = 750 THEN wh_per_km END AS "750 g",
  CASE WHEN flight = ${flight:raw} THEN wh_per_km END AS "Picked flight"
FROM $flights WHERE wh_per_km IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 1

spec.description: The wind the anemometer on board measured, averaged over the flight. It includes the airflow of the drone's own motion, so faster flights read windier.
spec.title: Energy per km against mean wind

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: one row per flight of CMU's package-delivery
-- quadcopter (DJI Matrice 100, Pittsburgh, April to October 2019; KiltHub,
-- CC BY 4.0), read through the gateway's month-long cache of flights.csv.
-- Energy is battery voltage × current integrated over each ~5 Hz step;
-- distance is the haversine sum of the GPS fixes. `altitude` is text because
-- two flights climb through a profile ("25-50-100-25").
WITH r AS (
  SELECT flight, time AS t, position_x AS lon, position_y AS lat, position_z AS z,
         battery_voltage * battery_current AS w, wind_speed,
         speed, payload, altitude, route, date, time_day
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/figshare/files/26385151', types = {'altitude': 'VARCHAR'})
),
s AS (
  SELECT *,
    t - lag(t) OVER f AS dt,
    2 * 6371000 * asin(sqrt(
      pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER f) / 2), 2) +
      cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER f)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER f) / 2), 2))) AS dm
  FROM r WINDOW f AS (PARTITION BY flight ORDER BY t)
)
SELECT
  flight,
  timezone('UTC', timezone('America/New_York', any_value(date) + CAST(any_value(time_day) AS TIME))) AS takeoff,
  any_value(route) AS route,
  any_value(speed) AS speed_ms,
  CAST(any_value(payload) AS INTEGER) AS payload_g,
  any_value(altitude) AS altitude_m,
  round(max(t)) AS duration_s,
  round(sum(dm)) AS distance_m,
  round(sum(w * dt) / 3600, 1) AS energy_wh,
  -- Hover and altitude tests (speed 0) barely move: no Wh/km for them.
  CASE WHEN any_value(speed) > 0 THEN round(sum(w * dt) / 3600 / (sum(dm) / 1000), 1) END AS wh_per_km,
  round(avg(wind_speed), 1) AS wind_ms,
  round(max(z) - arg_min(z, t)) AS max_height_m
FROM s GROUP BY flight ORDER BY flight

spec.sql:
-- Every flight, labelled by what was set for it: route, commanded speed,
-- payload and cruise altitude.
SELECT flight::INTEGER::VARCHAR AS value,
       '#' || flight::INTEGER || ' · ' || route || ' · ' || speed_ms::INTEGER || ' m/s · '
         || payload_g::INTEGER || ' g · ' || altitude_m || ' m' AS text
FROM $flights ORDER BY flight

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, on every change of flight: the picked flight only, about a
-- thousand rows at ~5 Hz, from the same cached flights.csv. `drone` is the
-- fleet layer's asset and `type` gives it the drone silhouette. Position is
-- longitude/latitude (position_x/y) and metres above sea level (position_z),
-- shown as height over the take-off point. Heading is the yaw of the
-- orientation quaternion as a compass bearing (it matches the GPS course in
-- cruise); speed is horizontal, from the velocity components. `time` is the
-- take-off's local time in Pittsburgh plus the seconds flown, in UTC.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT *, battery_voltage * battery_current * (time - coalesce(lag(time) OVER (ORDER BY time), time)) AS joules
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/figshare/files/26385151', types = {'altitude': 'VARCHAR'})
  WHERE flight = ${flight:raw}
)
SELECT
  timezone('UTC', timezone('America/New_York', date + CAST(time_day AS TIME)))
    + to_microseconds(CAST(round(time * 1e6) AS BIGINT)) AS time,
  round(time, 1) AS elapsed_s,
  'M100' AS drone,
  'drone' AS type,
  position_y AS latitude,
  position_x AS longitude,
  round(position_z - first(position_z) OVER w, 1) AS height_m,
  round((360 - degrees(atan2(2 * (orientation_w * orientation_z + orientation_x * orientation_y),
                             1 - 2 * (orientation_y * orientation_y + orientation_z * orientation_z)))) % 360) AS heading,
  round(3.6 * sqrt(velocity_x * velocity_x + velocity_y * velocity_y), 1) AS speed_kmh,
  round(battery_voltage, 2) AS voltage_v,
  round(battery_current, 2) AS current_a,
  round(battery_voltage * battery_current) AS power_w,
  round(sum(joules) OVER w / 3600, 2) AS energy_wh,
  round(wind_speed, 1) AS wind_ms,
  wind_angle AS wind_deg
FROM r WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY time)
ORDER BY time
